title: "Night Vision and Carotenoids"
brief_summary: Vision at twilight and night is more difficult and dangerous for the entire population, even more so for the elderly and especially for the elderly with degenerative disease. Multiple worldwide laboratories have demonstrated the ability to raise macular pigment optical density with dietary carotenoids. This proposal further evaluates the relationship between macular re- pigmentation and vision under stressed conditions simulating twilight and night driving.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* No significant supplementary carotenoids within last 10 weeks. Without significant media opacity, cataract or congenital / acquired retinal disease other than atrophic AMD or diabetic retinopathy. Minimum 20/25 to enroll.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Unwilling or medically / psychiatrically unable to take part in a 6 month study.
* Recent ophthalmologic surgery or treatment.
* Tricare, Retirees \& Enlisted Navy Personnel excluded. Already taking an OTC product to improve their night vision (containing carotenoids, polyphenols like bilberry).
